verdict_text:
NO

The merge computes the second task vector against the already-modified tensor rather than the unmodified base: it forms `tmp = b + λ(ft1 − b)` and then `out = tmp + λ(ft2 − tmp)`, so the second term is `λ(ft2 − tmp)` instead of `λ(ft2 − base)`. Algebraically the result is `(1−λ)·tmp + λ·ft2`, which differs from the required `base + λ(ft1 − base) + λ(ft2 − base)` by `λ²(ft1 − base)`, well outside the 1e-3 relative tolerance. This violates Required result step 2 and is exactly the ordering hazard the specification calls out. Everything else (name-set check, shared-tensor equality on the 180 non-MLP tensors, float32 compute with float16 cast, 64 merged and 244 output tensors, base tensors passed through unchanged) matches the specification.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
